quest.title: The City of Rains and Remembrance
quest.description: After a brisk meeting with the Hydro Archon, you decide to, at Lyney's invitation, attend his and Lynette's premiere magic performance at the opera house.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1125, Primogem x30, Mora x49200, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x9

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: This is our current abode.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Ah, Freminet, you're home. Where did everyone else go? I have some new friends that I would like to introduce.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Oh, they all just went out a moment ago.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I see. Everyone is getting busier now that "Father" will be returning soon. I suppose that can't be helped...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Allow me to introduce you to my little brother, Freminet. He is a phenomenal diver.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Uh, hello...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Nice to meet you! Paimon is Paimon, and this is {NICKNAME}. You sound very proud to have a diver as a brother, Lyney.

choices.text: Lyney sure seems to have a big family.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Haha...

response.speaker: Freminet
response.text: Uh, Lyney... Could you come here for a moment?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Hmm? What is it, Freminet? Do you have something to tell me?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's alright, you go ahead.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Hmm... Okay, I see.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is everything alright?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Oh, it's nothing, we were just discussing a little housework. Sorry for the interruption.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: #Before I forget, {NICKNAME} and I collected more materials to make Magic Pockets. Were you able to get any, Freminet?

response.speaker: Freminet
response.text: Yes, I went diving and gathered lots of materials. I was about to give them to you.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: That's our Freminet, always quick with the underwater work. Alright, I'll take these to the workshop.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: Looks like... rain.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, you're right. But wasn't it clear and sunny just a moment ago? Hmm... Fontaine's weather sure is weird.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Hehe, I'm afraid that's just how it is here. It often rains on days when there are trials being held in the opera house, but don't worry, it'll clear up soon enough.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm? What's wrong, Freminet?

response.speaker: Freminet
response.text: There's a legend about the rain that I tend to believe...

response.speaker: Freminet
response.text: It's said that a Dragon of Water once resided in Fontaine. Though we don't know where the dragon went, every time it weeps, the skies will cloud up and pour out rain.

response.speaker: Freminet
response.text: When I was a child, my mother told me that if I wanted to go outside and play, I should yell toward the sky at the top of my lungs...

response.speaker: Freminet
response.text: "Hydro Dragon, Hydro Dragon, don't cry!"

choices.text: Could that Hydro Dragon be the elemental dragon of Fontaine?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If it's an elemental dragon, then having the power to make it rain wouldn't be very unusual.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let Paimon try something...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Hydro Dragon, Hydro Dragon, don't cry!"

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Heh... doesn't seem to be of any use. It is just a legend, after all.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: You know, you might be a more popular magician if you understood the concept of "romanticism"... or could at least play along.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Sorry! It might be because we've never met the Hydro Dragon. Perhaps it can't be comforted by the words of strangers.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: After some time, the rain stops.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: It rained for longer than I suspected... Uh, it's already getting late.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Was there something you needed to do, Lyney?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Yeah, some preparations for the show at the opera house. I need to find a way to catch the last aquabus of the day.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: On the day of the performance, just ride the aquabus to the island of Erinnyes. I'll have Lynette meet you at the fountain in front of the opera house.

choices.text: Sounds good. You go ahead, Lyney.

response.speaker: Freminet
response.text: Oh, uh... Are you leaving now?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: What is it, Freminet? I'm in a hurry. Oh, I get it. You feel nervous delivering the materials for the Magic Pockets, is that it?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: #Perhaps we could trouble {NICKNAME} to help us take these materials to the Beaumont Workshop and deliver them to the owner there?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I'm afraid that Freminet can be quite introverted... And the boss there tends to be pretty talkative. Freminet has always been a little afraid of her.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No trouble at all. Don't worry, we're on the case!

response.speaker: Freminet
response.text: Sorry for the inconvenience. I'm quite useless when it comes to such tasks... I'll think of a way to make it up to you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, no need, no need! This'll be a walk in the park for us.

choices.text: See you at the performance.
Another one of the elemental dragons of Teyvat...
What a talented family.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello? Is there anyone here?

dialogues.speaker: Estelle
dialogues.text: Oh, hello there. New customers? Looking to buy, or do you need something made? Or perhaps you're just looking for a chat with me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh — no, we're just here to deliver some materials. Here they are. They're for making... uh, what were they called again?

dialogues.speaker: Estelle
dialogues.text: Ah, these must be for Magic Pockets. I could tell right away, I've already made several orders' worth now.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do we need to pay?

dialogues.speaker: Estelle
dialogues.text: No, no need. They've already prepaid several batches worth. When they told me what they'd be using them for, I even offered them a discount.

dialogues.speaker: Estelle
dialogues.text: But they insisted on paying the full amount, saying that I had a business to run... Hehe, it seems both their hearts and their pockets are made of gold.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, so is Lyney actually loaded?

dialogues.speaker: Estelle
dialogues.text: I can't say for sure, but who knows... Maybe there's good money to be made being a magician in Fontaine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, is this machine what you use to make stuff here? It looks really advanced...

dialogues.speaker: Estelle
dialogues.text: Why use your hands when a machine can do the work? It would be a waste not to use the latest technology, and wasting is a kind of crime.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But where does a big machine like that get its power from?

dialogues.speaker: Estelle
dialogues.text: Ah, well... It's a little complicated, I'm not sure I can put it in layman's terms for you...

dialogues.speaker: Estelle
dialogues.text: But basically, everything we usually use here in the city is powered by Indemnitium. It's a type of energy that's produced from trials.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? How can trials produce energy?

dialogues.speaker: Estelle
dialogues.text: Well, I'm not completely sure of all the details myself, but basically...

dialogues.speaker: Estelle
dialogues.text: When a trial is in session, the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale harvests people's belief in justice, and converts it into energy to be used all around Fontaine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So that's what its other function is? Paimon heard that the Oratrice was created by the Archon to make judgments.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But Paimon still doesn't get it. How could something unreliable like people's beliefs be turned into a stable power source for these machines?

choices.text: Well, Venti and Nahida both said...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, yeah! So that means the Hydro Archon relies on the machine to take the energy created by belief and turn it into power for all of Fontaine, right?

response.speaker: Estelle
response.text: Even though I've never heard anyone really put it that way before, it sounds like it makes sense.

response.speaker: Estelle
response.text: Besides Indemnitium, we have another type of energy called "Pneumousia."

response.speaker: Estelle
response.text: It isn't produced by the power of the Archon, but it is unstable by nature. Even now it still cannot be widely used by civilians.

response.speaker: Truand
response.text: Heh, I thought I'd find you hard at work, but here you are chatting the day away... Since you're already talking, I'm sure you wouldn't mind a few words with me.

response.speaker: Estelle
response.text: Y—You again? Didn't I already promise you that I'd have the Mora I owe to Confrerie of Cabriere by next month? Why are you hounding me now?

response.speaker: Truand
response.text: Yeah, but how do we know that you won't go running off by the end of this month? I want fifty percent. Today. Wait, no... seventy percent.

response.speaker: Estelle
response.text: Huh!? You...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Seems business isn't so great for the workshop... We've already finished our job and delivered the materials. Maybe now's a good time to leave?

choices.text: You're right.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Hey, hold on! Before you go around trying to collect payments, why don't you settle your own debts first?

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: If Confrerie of Cabriere wants to poach clients from Northland Bank, that's fine, but I'm afraid you still owe the bank a hefty sum of Mora. So why don't we work things out between us first before you get back to your little conversation here?

response.speaker: Truand
response.text: Ah, you're from Northland Bank? But we said we'll pay everything we owe next month. Why are you hounding me now?

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: #Oh, {NICKNAME}! Paimon! I didn't think I'd run into you here in Fontaine. What are the chances!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We're surprised to see you too! What are you doing here in Fontaine? You didn't want to stay in Snezhnaya?

choices.text: We sure seem to have run into a lot of friends today.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Haha! Long story short, I've already been in Fontaine for some time now, and honestly, things have been pretty boring.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: But it seems that fate brought our paths together today. Not only will I have some good friends here now, but ones who always seem to find trouble.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Either way you look at it, it seems things are going to get a lot more interesting now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Pretty sure we'd want to avoid anything that you'd find interesting... Besides, our trip here has gone pretty well so far, right {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: I think we've already weathered enough storms for now.

response.speaker: Truand
response.text: Ahem, uh... Hey you, Northland Bank boy. Aren't you forgetting something?

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: #Don't interrupt. It's not often I run into {NICKNAME} like this. Why don't you wait for me over there for a while?

response.speaker: Truand
response.text: You kidding? Aren't you the one looking for us? You really expect us to sit and twiddle our thumbs while you catch up with your friends?

response.speaker: Truand
response.text: Listen to me, boy. If you want your Mora, fine — why don't you come and take it?

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: #Hey, I just said not to interrupt. Oh, by the way, {NICKNAME}... The last time I took Tonia and Teucer ice fishing, Teucer said...

response.speaker: Truand
response.text: HEY!!! That's way over the line! Alright, boys! Let's see who has to pay up now!

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Ugh, can't you at least let me finish one sentence? Fine, though the bank told me not to get rough with our clients...

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: You're the ones who started it! This is an act of self-defense. You two will have to be my witnesses, okay?

choices.text: Okay, sure.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's sure this won't take long.

choices.text: Go ahead, they're all yours.
I don't mind a little excitement every now and then.
Fontaine really is a curious place.
Sounds like a usual case of someone owing somebody else money.
The gods rely on belief to obtain power.

talks.objective: Defeat the Confrerie of Cabriere henchmen

dialogues.speaker: Truand
dialogues.text: What's your deal, brat...? How are you so strong if you're just a staffer from Snezhnaya's Northland Bank? ...Wait, don't tell me you're—!

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Oh, now you notice? It's a little late, don't you think? Just make sure you understand that you don't mess with Northland Bank, got it?

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: ...Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Truand
dialogues.text: Now's my chance!

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Huh... That was weird...

choices.text: What just happened?

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: I'm not sure... It's as if I suddenly lost control of my Hydro powers when I needed them. Maybe there's something wrong with my Vision?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Strange, how could that happen? First time Paimon's ever heard of someone losing control of their Vision.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Never mind, it doesn't matter. If I wanna stay sharp, I shouldn't be relying too much on my Vision anyway. Besides, I always have my Delusion in case I need it.

choices.text: You'd better not use your Delusion too often.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So what are you doing in Fontaine, Childe? And don't say it's work for Northland Bank!

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Well... I guess it's because I've been in a bad mood lately.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What kind of reason is that? Wait, since when do you feel down about anything?

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Haha, I dunno... Maybe I still have a lot to learn about myself.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: But recently, there seems to be some sort of restless power stirring inside of me... And I don't know why, but every now and then I feel like I'm in a terrible mood...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Maybe you losing control of your Vision just now is connected with that power you're feeling inside?

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Hmm, that is a possibility.

choices.text: So about this power...

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: I can't remember if I've ever mentioned it before, but when I was fourteen, I fell into some unknown abyss...

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: It was during that time I learned nearly all of my abilities. The one who took me under her wing and taught me was named Skirk.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: She was always quiet and very mysterious. Nobody knew where she came from or what she had been through, and she was always very strict when teaching me combat techniques.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: One time, I asked her why she was willing to take me on as an apprentice. From what I could make of her answer, it was...

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Because I had awakened "it," and traces of "it" remained on me. She said that all my combat training would be useful in the future.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But what is "it"? What did you awaken?

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: She never explained that, but my guess is that it's related to a dream I saw when I had just fallen into that abyss.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: In my dream, I was in the deepest depths of the sea, and the boundless seabed was all around me. But in front of me appeared a whale that was so massive I felt like I couldn't breathe.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A whale? Oh, that sounds familiar... When we fought against you before, you summoned a huge whale that seemed to leap at us! Is that the one?

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Hehe, that's just an abstract form of a whale that I create using my elemental powers.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: It takes that shape because the scene I dreamt of the whale has always been stuck in my mind. I'll never forget it...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you used the whale as inspiration for one of your moves? Huh... Seems a little twisted to Paimon.

choices.text: It's very possible that...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So why don't you just go ask your master? Maybe she knows the answer.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: You make it sound so easy. Ever since the incident I experienced there, I've never stopped searching for Master Skirk and that unknown abyss.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: But it's been years now and I've still found nothing. There isn't even a trace of the place where I remember falling into the abyss.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, it sounds like some kind of ghost story.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Yeah, I'm out of leads at this point, but there's nothing more I can do. It seems that strange encounters in this world tend to be elusive like that.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Oh, seems the time really flies when I'm talking with you... I just remembered I have somewhere else I need to be, so I should get going.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What, more work for the Northland Bank?

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: No, it's more of a personal appointment. Lately, I've been sparring with some of Fontaine's official Champion Duelists whenever I'm feeling bored.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Official Champion Duelists? You mean it's their job to duel?

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Yep. In Fontaine, before a criminal goes to court, they're given one chance to defend their honor by requesting a duel with an official Champion Duelist.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: The Champion Duelists are all powerful fighters selected from among the nation's best, and the duel itself is a no holds barred fight with no specified stopping point...

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: So engaging in such a duel is regarded as a symbol of defending your honor. If a criminal manages to win the duel, they'll be acquitted, but if they lose, they'll have no choice but to stand trial.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: And the worst case scenario is that you're simply killed in the duel.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Though it's rumored that Fontaine has a death penalty, from what I can tell, no one has ever been officially sentenced to death.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: So really, the only people who opt to duel are those who have suffered a grave injustice in being accused, or those who greatly value their honor. Otherwise, why gamble with your life?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So do many people actually get out of their trials by winning the duel?

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Apparently it's exceedingly rare for anyone to actually win. Fontaine probably enacted this system as a way to show that the nation respects the honor of its citizens.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Besides, none of the Champion Duelists are to be trifled with... Which is exactly why I was itching to face them as soon as I got to Fontaine.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Apparently the one I'm meeting today, Clorinde, is the strongest of the Champion Duelists. I had been asking her for some time before she finally agreed to face me today.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, that's Childe for ya... Paimon feels like we've heard that name somewhere before. Clorinde, huh...

choices.text: When we met the Hydro Archon.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Oh, before I forget, I want you to have this.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Your Vision! You're seriously just giving it away!?

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: I'm just worried that it could become uncontrollable again. I'd be pretty upset if it got in the way of my duel, so I think I'll be better off without it for now.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Besides, I just need you to hold onto it for a short while. I'll come retrieve it when I have some time later.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon knows what you're up to! You just want an excuse to come talk to us again, don't you?

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Haha, whatever gave you that idea? I'll be in touch, later.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, that sneaky guy... He said he's been feeling down lately, but he seemed the same as ever to Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, seems we don't have much to do for now... We might as well walk around and see the city before Lyney's performance!

choices.text: I'm terrible at remembering names.
The power inside you is connected to your incident in the abyss.
Do you have any idea where it came from?
I don't have a Vision, so don't ask me.
Are you feeling alright?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, who could have seen that coming!? The reporter who was barely around for most of the story was the murderer all along!

choices.text: Hey, don't blurt it out, Paimon...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, sorry... Paimon was just surprised, that's all. Whew, Paimon never saw that twist coming... The murder mystery novels here are amazing!

choices.text: Never thought I'd see the day when Paimon would enjoy reading...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The whodunits here in Fontaine are a lot different than the light novels you see from Yae Publishing House. Both have their merits, but Paimon thinks this style of novels are more... well, novel!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's so exciting to reach the moment when the mystery is uncovered! Especially in the one Paimon was just reading, you should buy a copy and read it, too!

choices.text: I'm good.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, sorry about that... Paimon will be more careful next time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, shouldn't we be heading to the opera house to see Lyney's performance soon? It's almost time for the show to start, so we should get going.

choices.text: You already spoiled who the murderer is.
Do you have any idea how long we were loitering here...
It's rude to spoil the mystery for everyone else.

talks.objective: Ride the Navia Line and head to Erinnyes
Ride the Navia Line and head to Erinnyes
Go to the fountain plaza in front of the opera house

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, now this is fancy! The Opera Epiclese... What a place to hold a performance, no wonder Lyney and Lynette were looking forward to it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Looks like there's a lot of people standing around the fountain up ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Joliot
dialogues.text: O Archon... please bless us with a bright and healthy child. We pray—

dialogues.speaker: Irimia
dialogues.text: ...I don't know why you always feel the need to ask so much... I'll be happy as long as our child is healthy, and lives a peaceful life.

dialogues.speaker: Joliot
dialogues.text: Hehe, I guess if they're our kid, then there's no doubt they'll turn out smart.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe this is one of the customs in Fontaine? There sure are a lot of couples here...
"Vacher..."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's wrong?
"Vacher... Vacher..."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did you just say something, Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No, Paimon didn't say anything. Are you hearing things?

choices.text: Strange...

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: Welcome to the Fountain of Lucine. All the water flowing through Fontaine converges here. It's customary for newlyweds to come here and wish for children.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Waah! Lynette! You scared Paimon! When did you get here?

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: Lyney asked me to wait here for you, remember?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, right...

choices.text: By the way, Lynette...

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: What do you mean? There are a lot of people here right now.

choices.text: It seemed as if...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh!? Hey, you're not trying to scare Paimon, are you? Besides, it's the middle of the day, it's not the time for eerie things...

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: Hmm, I see... I might be able to tell you something that could help explain the voice you heard.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: In fact, you might not be imagining things at all. I suspect that what you heard is a result of your hypersensitivity to the Hydro element. Others in my family have had similar experiences.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #It's because of {M#his}{F#her} sensitivity to the Hydro element? But what would hearing a voice have to do with elemental power?

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: When do you cry, Paimon?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, what? What does that have to do with anything?

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: Just answer me. When do you cry?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, when Paimon's really sad... Oh, and when Paimon's super happy. Oh, and also when Paimon's really, really scared.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: Then you should understand that tears... contain your most intense emotions.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: Like I just mentioned, the Fountain of Lucine is where all the flowing water in Fontaine converges. Even the tears that fall to the ground will eventually gather here.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: So maybe what you heard was the intense emotion coming from someone's tears.

choices.text: Huh, that's an interesting explanation.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So what did the voice say?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It seemed to be calling out someone's name.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, if you were hearing their emotions, then Paimon wonders what happened to them.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: Rather than worrying about them, we should worry about my brother first.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: Don't let that calm look of his fool you, he tends to get pretty nervous just before a performance. So chatting with Lyney might help him relax a little before he goes on stage.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh right, that makes sense. Let's go in and see Lyney!

choices.text: (I'm not sure whether I buy it, though...)
The voice was coming from the fountain.
I seemed to hear a faint voice just now.
Whose voice was that just now...?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: #Ah, {NICKNAME} and Paimon, good to see you. I knew you two would come.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you kidding? We wouldn't miss it for the world. We've been looking forward to it!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Hehe. I can tell, judging by how early you've arrived.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: But you're actually right on time. The audience still hasn't started entering the venue yet, which means now is the perfect chance for us to take you to the best seats in the house. Wait just a moment, I'll fetch the tickets.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: The opera house has assigned seating, so you always have to make reservations. I've already reserved your seats, and here are your tickets.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh! Front row seats! Thanks, Lyney!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Don't mention it, there's no need to keep thanking me...

dialogues.speaker: Cowell
dialogues.text: Hey, Lyney! Could you come over here and take a look at this?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Oh, I'll be right there. Seems there's an issue with the stage props over there. That's Cowell, my assistant, calling me. I'll go lend him a hand.

choices.text: Sure.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, we'll just go to our seats. You go ahead, Lyney.

choices.text: Best get busy.

talks.objective: Go to the seats Lyney arranged

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, these should be our seats. C'mon, let's sit down.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Heh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hey, {NICKNAME}... Maybe we should strike up a conversation with the person next to us? Since we're sitting together and the rest of the place is practically empty still, it's kinda awkward if we don't say anything.

choices.text: You're up, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You little... Of course you put this on Paimon...
Excuse me, I did not realize you felt awkward. I am terribly sorry.
I would be perfectly happy to chat with you if that's what you would like.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh... uh... So you heard all of that, did ya? Boy, you sure have good ears, Paimon thought she was keeping her voice down.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah! Wait, that's not it, Paimon's sorry! Um, Paimon's the one who was being rude talking under her breath like that. Uh, so let's talk, but... uh... what should we talk about?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (This is getting even more awkward...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Oh, Paimon's got it! You're also here early and sitting in the front. Are you a friend of Lyney's, too?
A... friend, you say? Well, if Mr. Lyney would like to be my friend, I would be more than happy to reciprocate.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, so you're not friends with Lyney, then... Whew, this is getting more awkward by the second. Ah, Paimon nearly forgot to make our introduction...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Nice to meet you, Paimon is Paimon, and this is {NICKNAME}. We just arrived in Fontaine.
It is an honor to meet you two. I have heard of your deeds across Teyvat.
And as required by proper etiquette, I will also introduce myself. I am...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Oh, Monsieur Neuvillette! What an honor it is to have you here to see my show!

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Ah, Mr. Lyney. I should say it is in fact an honor for me to see your performance in person.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, Neuvillette? Could he be...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Hmm? I saw you all chatting just now, but it seems you still don't know who Monsieur Neuvillette is.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Allow me to introduce you to Fontaine's Chief J{RUBY#[S]Iudex}ustice. That seat is always reserved for him. It wouldn't be too much to say that he's the symbol of justice and honesty here in Fontaine.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa! Sorry for being so rude just now. Paimon had no idea you were such an important person...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: No offense taken. Being Chief J{RUBY#[S]Iudex}ustice is merely what I do for work. Nearly every person has their usual reserved seat, so I am not so special, really.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: And by the way, I should probably let you know, even though I would prefer not to...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: There's someone sitting up there in the VIP seats that has been striking a pose for quite a while now...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: I believe she's trying to give you a most elegant and impressive first impression.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: So I think you should take notice of her sooner rather than later, otherwise she may become flustered.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Hehehehe...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Oh, it's Furina, the Hydro Archon. She sure has a smug and satisfied look on her face. Guess she has no idea that you saw right through her act.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Very good, that is for the best. No need to pay her any more attention, we may now enjoy the show.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, so is this what things are like between the Chief Justice and the Hydro Archon?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Alright, please wait just a moment longer. I've pretty much finished my preparations and the performance will start as soon as the audience has made their way to their seats.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yay, the show's finally about to start. Ooh, Paimon can hardly wait! Paimon's never seen a real live magic show before!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: The crowds enter the venue, and the curtains open for the show to begin...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! They're dimming the lights, the show must be starting!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah... sorry. Paimon will try to stay quiet, hehe.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Welcome, one and all, to the Opera Epiclese! I am the star of today's show, Lyney!

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: And over here is my sister, Lynette, who will be working as my wonderful assistant. Please, let's give her a warm welcome!

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: Hello, everyone.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Haha, I know she may seem to be a little sleepy right now, but that's just a sign that she's nervous.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: Whatever.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Now, some of you may be thinking: Two Vision holders who can freely manipulate elemental powers performing magic is not true magic at all.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: So, I would like to take a moment to assure you that elemental powers will have nothing to do with what you will witness on the stage today.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Both Lynette and myself have removed our Visions for the show. That way, even the gods won't be able to help us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, good point. That's what makes the show real magic!

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Now, without further ado, let the show begin! Lynette will now exit the stage to make some preparations.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I know you might miss her, but don't worry, she'll be coming right back on stage momentarily... Perhaps in an unexpected way. I'm sure she'll be stealing the spotlight soon enough.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Oh, and before I forget... There's one more thing I should say.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: You never know what can happen in the blink of an eye.

choices.text: Isn't that usually your job?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! What in the world just happened!? How did he do that!? Paimon didn't see him do anything!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wasn't Lynette inside the water tank? How did she disappear and then reappear out of nowhere!?

choices.text: What a show!

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: If we could see easily through his tricks, then that would mean that his skills are still lacking.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: To appreciate magic, you should focus on the show happening on stage rather than getting caught up in trying to see that which has been intentionally hidden.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, guess you're right. Paimon couldn't believe her eyes when Lynette reappeared. Amazing!

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Thank you, thank you, everyone. I'm glad you enjoyed that performance...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: But our magical journey has only just begun. I've prepared even more astonishing surprises for everyone here.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: The magic of transformation and disappearance can go far beyond what you've just seen.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I'm sure many of you are thinking that escaping the water tank was impressive enough, but Lynette is still my assistant, after all.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: In which case, I have ample time to make all necessary preparations.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: So for my next trick, I will require the participation of one lucky audience member.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Please, if my assistants could bring out the magical boxes now...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: There are two boxes, and only two boxes. One is here, and one is there in the aisle among the audience.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I'm sure many of our clever audience members have already guessed our next magic trick. A swap!

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Our lucky audience member and I will each enter a magic box. After one minute, we will each emerge from the opposite box.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Now please, everyone pay very close attention to the box you see here. Don't give me any chance to make a move!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow! How's he gonna do this?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, do you think this is all magic tricks, or does Lyney have actual superpowers?

choices.text: Let's watch and see.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: The lucky audience member will be generated by this random number selector.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: It selects numbers entirely at random. Even I don't know who will be chosen to participate.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Now then, let's begin.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Ah, let me see... row seven, seat three. Congratulations! You now have the chance to experience magic firsthand for an entire minute!

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Please, come forward. My assistant will take you beside the magic box.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I'm sorry, it might be a little cramped inside, but no need to feel nervous. We've carefully arranged everything for you to be as comfortable as possible.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: You don't need to do anything. But no matter what strange things may happen, don't come out of the box.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: If the magic is interrupted, who knows where you might end up? You might even find yourself in the Fortress of Meropide.

response.speaker: Audience
response.text: Oh, okay...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Alright, before I enter the magic box, there is one more thing I need to ask the audience to do. Could you all give me a countdown?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Like this... Sixty, fifty-nine, fifty-eight... Just keep counting down. You can go a little faster or slower if you like.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I won't be able to see anything in the pitch-black box, so I'll be relying on your voices to know when time is up.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Oh, and no tricks now. If you quickly count from sixty in just thirty seconds, then I'll be in a tough spot.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, Paimon kinda wants to count faster after hearing him say that, hehe...

choices.text: I'm sure Lyney's prepared.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: No, no, that won't do... I can see it in your eyes, you still can't be trusted! Let's practice together.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Come on, repeat after me. Sixty, fifty-nine, fifty-eight...

response.speaker: Crowd
response.text: Sixty, fifty-nine, fifty-eight...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: That's right, perfect! Keep it going! Alright, I'll see you all on the other side once you've finished counting.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Fifty-four, fifty-three, fifty-two...!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why aren't you counting, Neuvillette?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: I'm counting in my head. I think things are exciting enough in here as it is.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Merely a consequence of my identity and personality. Do not worry about me. Just enjoy the show.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, alright. You looked so serious that Paimon thought you might be feeling uncomfortable or something.

response.speaker: Crowd
response.text: Forty, thirty-nine, thirty-eight!

response.speaker: Garrick
response.text: Mr. Lyney, are you all right in there? Is everything ready?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Yes, I'm fine, I'm fine... I'm just double checking the direction of the magic.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: It would be a disaster if we get sent to the wrong places, for example, mid-air right above the audience.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Even though he's saying that, Lyney doesn't seem nervous at all.

choices.text: I think it's all part of the show.

response.text: BANG!!!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What was that noise? Did you hear it, too?

choices.text: Did it come from the stage?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Not sure... Anyway, it doesn't seem like anyone's worried about it.

response.speaker: Crowd
response.text: Twenty-five, twenty-four, twenty-three!

response.speaker: Garrick
response.text: What's wrong, Mr. Lyney? I can still hear you moving in there.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I seem to have accidentally knocked over a decoration. I'm trying to fix it, but it's pitch black in here, I can't tell left from right.

response.speaker: Garrick
response.text: Never mind the decorations, there's no time for that. The show is what's important.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: No, that's unacceptable, I want my show to be perfect. Don't worry, we still have twenty seconds. Hear them counting?

response.speaker: Crowd
response.text: Nineteen, eighteen, seventeen!

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Ah, it seems things aren't quite going as planned. I apologize, everyone.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: It feels like you're all starting to count faster, but that's alright. I know it can be tiring to do such a long countdown.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Ten seconds and change is still plenty of time.

choices.text: Maybe it was just to divert our attention.
Maybe he's just supremely confident in his abilities.
With the whole crowd counting together, you couldn't even if you wanted to.
I'm sure we can spot how he does it...
No wonder he's a famous magician.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Huh!?

dialogues.speaker: Excited Audience Member
dialogues.text: Is this... part of the show?

dialogues.speaker: Excited Audience Member
dialogues.text: Mr. Lyney, you're going to use magic to fix the stage now, right?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: What happened...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no, maybe this isn't part of the show... The girl was still in that box, right?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: This performance is over! Medical staff, with me. Gardes, secure the scene and detain all the performers. Seal the exits, no one is allowed in or out at this time!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Yes, th—that's right! If this was just an accident, then we must investigate the cause. But if this was all part of some scheme, then... then those accountable will not escape the judgment of the God of Justice!

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: No need to be alarmed, you two. We'll get to the bottom of this soon enough.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After some time, the Gardes complete their investigation.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, the person who was in the magic box has been pronounced dead. His name was Cowell, one of the assistants in Lyney's magic troupe.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Apparently, the fireworks on stage ignited the ropes that were suspending the water tank, which then caused the tank to fall onto the stage.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: As of now, we are still not sure why we found Cowell in the box rather than the guest from the audience.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: And after an initial search of the area, the Gardes have confirmed that the girl is nowhere to be found.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: It appears that this incident was not merely some mishap with the performance.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: And there are many indications that it is connected with the case of the serial disappearances of young women.

dialogues.speaker: Surprised Audience Member
dialogues.text: Th—The serial disappearances case!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, that's the case that Charlotte mentioned before!

choices.text: And to pull it off like this...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Hehe. I know, I know the truth! I can see through the whole thing... Really, using such a shallow and obvious mystery as his "finale"... Did he really underestimate us that badly?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I say that our powerful magician, Mr. Lyney, is now the prime suspect for the serial disappearances case.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Huh, why me? This whole thing was an accident!

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: This all occurred during your magic show, did it not? The missing girl disappeared after being chosen, did she not? The deceased is one of your assistants, is he not?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Now that I think about it, that whole speech about magicians making things disappear was nothing more than a provocation, a bald-faced challenge!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That can't be right... How could Lyney do this?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He was in the box on stage the entire time. We could even hear his voice.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Besides, before the show he told us that he would like to catch the criminal behind the disappearances. He couldn't possibly mean catching himself!

choices.text: He's a suspect at most.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Save discussion for a later time, please. Lady Furina, may I assume that your comments just now constitute an accusation against Mr. Lyney and his associates and that you are pressing charges?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Huh? I just think that he... Well, I, ah, think it might be a little early to talk about formally pressing charges...

response.speaker: Excited Audience Member
response.text: But what Lady Furina said just now makes perfect sense! Looks like she's gonna personally deliver justice!

response.speaker: Admiring Audience Member
response.text: A kidnapping and murder carried out under the cover of a magic show. Lady Furina said it all.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: *cough* Ahem, uh... I mean... of course, my dear people! But what excites me even more than the obvious truth before our eyes... is the opponent I'll be facing.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: That's right, I mean you, Traveler. You'll support Lyney, won't you? After all, he was the one who helped you the first time we met.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I trust Lyney.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Haha, then there's no problem at all. You know, the Traveler and I already had a duel the first time we met.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: But with Lyney's help, our little duel ended in a draw! Hehe... But draws really are the most boring possible outcome...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: So no more draws! Between the two of us, there must be a clear winner and loser. And what better place to hold such a riveting showdown and decide the true victor than here, on the grandest of stages, the Opera Epiclese!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? It wasn't a draw, she obviously lost last time...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: I understand. Charges have now been pressed, and as such, a trial is in order.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: #Well, {NICKNAME}, seems Lady Furina has set you in her sights. But, putting her dramatic rhetoric aside for a moment, I would like to ask you...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Are you willing to act as Mr. Lyney's attorney and defend him in this case?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yes, I am.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Very well. The trial will be held a day from now in the opera house. Both sides may investigate the scene to build their cases and search for the truth.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Lyney and his troupe are all potential suspects and shall remain within the opera house.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: The audience may begin to leave in an orderly fashion once they have been cleared by the Gardes.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: A day isn't that long. Let's see what kind of case this big-shot outlander can build in such a short amount of time. Hehehe, I'm really quite looking forward to hearing it.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Everyone is dismissed and the audience begins to leave along with Furina and Neuvillette.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Lyney!

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Sorry about everything that happened just now, were you frightened?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Of course, who wouldn't be scared after witnessing an accident like that?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Yeah, I'm a little shaken up myself... How could this happen? And poor Cowell...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I know you already claimed that you would defend me, but now it's just us talking... Tell me, do you think I could possibly be the murderer?

choices.text: No.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Good to hear... Thank you so much for trusting me.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I'm sure everyone sees me as the biggest suspect at this point. But if you ask me, the whole thing is mysteries layered upon mysteries, such that all that's left is confusion.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I don't know whether what happened there on the stage was purely an accident or not... and I don't know why poor Cowell was in the box.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: As for how that girl chosen from the audience could suddenly disappear, I'm afraid I don't have any answers, either. If someone tampered with my performance, then we need to figure out what they did.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Even a skilled and knowledgeable magician like myself couldn't pull all that off in just one minute.

choices.text: Yes, it is very strange.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Which is precisely why we need to investigate. As this book says, "The impossible could not have happened. Whatever happened must have been that which is possible."

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Where did you get those glasses?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon bought them when we were reading at the bookshop in the city earlier. Pretty cool, huh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't worry, Paimon used her own savings to buy them. It wasn't from our travel funds.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: I think they look cute on you, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You have good taste, Lynette. Hehe!

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Haha, that's the right attitude. Feeling depressed isn't going to help me now, I need to get back to my normal self.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: But with the Gardes watching our every move, it's going to be especially difficult for Lynette and I to prove our own innocence.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Good thing you agreed to be our attorneys, thanks for that. We'll be counting on you.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: Yes, thank you so much.

choices.text: I won't let you down.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, just leave it to us!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, since we're going to start investigating, Paimon has a question first. Where did Lynette go during the performance?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Ah, well... I'm afraid that would involve some of our essential trade secrets as magicians...

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: The secrets behind our magic are past saving, Lyney.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I suppose you're right. The truth behind our tricks is going to be important evidence that will be weighed during the trial.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Ah! 'Tis truly a pity. As a magician, our magic show is a work of art. We've poured countless hours and spared no effort in perfecting it.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: But if revealing our secrets will help you uncover the truth behind what happened, then it will be well worth it.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: We should go somewhere else if we're going to discuss our magic tricks. We'll go speak with the Gardes, and in the meantime, you can go investigate the stage and the seating areas.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, let's go have a look while the investigation teams are still here. Detective Paimon is on the case!

choices.text: I'm used to this sort of thing.
But there's no denying what happened.
It's hard to say...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I understand. Even I'm not sure what happened, so I can only imagine how difficult it is for you to grasp the situation.

choices.text: It's hard to believe all this happened during the show.
In front of an audience including the Archon and Chief Justice.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Thanks again, you two. I really can't deal with that lady...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Under Paimon's enthusiastic leadership, you walk all around the Court of Fontaine...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Lyney said that the opera house is on Erinnyes, so let's go ride the aquabus!
